QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_49

question.text: The core rationale of the Social Stock Exchange as articulated in Chapter 2 is to:

answer.text: Create a regulated arbitrage venue for impact bonds.
Bridge the gap between the private sector and non-profit sector for utilisation of resources, channelling greater capital to FPEs and non-profit sector providers.
Enable NPOs to speculate on listed equities to generate endowment returns.
Consolidate all CSR spending through a single mandatory exchange.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.1.2, 'the rationale of SSE has several different aspects. Most importantly it bridges the gap between the private sector and non-profit sector for utilisation of these resources. The SSE is meant to serve the FPEs and non-profit sector providers by channelling greater capital to them.' This is the foundational policy intent. The Trap: Option A misreads 'impact venue' as 'arbitrage venue'. Option C reverses the flow (NPOs are recipients, not speculators). Option D overstates — CSR retains multiple legitimate channels outside SSE. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C (Compliance) treat CSR Section 135 routes. V-A/X-A/X-B treat donor-side channel choice. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When writing the 'Context' paragraph of your SIR, anchor your framing to the 'bridging gap between private and non-profit sectors' language — this mirrors the regulator's policy intent and strengthens the document's reception by SEBI reviewers and listing exchanges.
